scope: Proposition 3.6 (Attachment moments) of the manuscript “Critical honeycomb chords with prescribed boundary endpoints” (preprints/Critical-honeycomb-chords-with-prescribed-boundary-endpoints-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 237 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 6b7adfc0aa278ae3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 10. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let E be an event of input chords from a to the stated terminal interval, of critical mass E. The fixed-source attachment construction just described has a translation count Ns on output chords and critical output measure µa such that Z Ns dµa ≥ cs1/2 E, Z N2 s dµa ≤ CsR−1/4 . (3.5) Here the side-1 outer landing is exactly a; the side-2 outer landing is free on its support. The estimate applies also to input chords in the full two-cut domain, without a diameter bound. If the input chords lie in a convex pure domain of diameter O(R), there is also a construction at scale s = cR with both outer landings free, all outputs in one convex pure domain of diameter O(R), and Z Nfree R dµfree ≥ cR3/2 E, Z (Nfree R )2 dµfree ≤ CR7/4 . (3.6) The measure µfree sums critical weights over ordered output endpoint pairs. In both constructions output length is the input length plus the two attached lengths. Constants are uniform for fixed compact endpoint geometries and independent of the fixed length slack δ; the required lower threshold for s may depend on δ.
